threads.body: Tool definitions are captured even when capture_content is False. Since util-genai can still emit gen_ai.tool.definitions even when message content capture is disabled, this can unintentionally record tool schemas/params despite OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=NO_CONTENT and no completion hook.

+
+def extract_server_address_and_port(
+    endpoint_url: str | None,
+) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
+    """Parse server address and port from a client endpoint URL."""
+    if not endpoint_url:
+        return None, None
+    parsed = urlparse(endpoint_url)
+    server_address = parsed.hostname
+    server_port = parsed.port
+    if server_port is None and parsed.scheme in ("http", "https"):
+        server_port = 443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80
+    return server_address, server_port
+
+
+def extract_content_block(block: dict[str, Any]) -> MessagePart | None:
+    """Map a single Bedrock content block to an OpenTelemetry MessagePart."""
+    if "text" in block:
+        return Text(content=block["text"])
+
+    image = block.get("image")
+    if _is_dict(image):
+        fmt = image.get("format", "jpeg")
+        source = image.get("source")
+        content_bytes = source.get("bytes", b"") if _is_dict(source) else b""
+        return Blob(
+            content=content_bytes,
+            mime_type=f"image/{fmt}",
+            modality="image",

+
+    tool_use = block.get("toolUse")

+            arguments=tool_use.get("input"),

+    tool_result = block.get("toolResult")
+    if _is_dict(tool_result):

+    inf_config = kwargs.get("inferenceConfig")
+    if _is_dict(inf_config):
+        invocation.temperature = inf_config.get("temperature")
+        invocation.top_p = inf_config.get("topP")
+        invocation.max_tokens = inf_config.get("maxTokens")
+        invocation.stop_sequences = inf_config.get("stopSequences")
+        invocation.top_k = inf_config.get("topK") or inf_config.get("top_k")
+        invocation.seed = inf_config.get("seed")
+
+    add_fields = kwargs.get("additionalModelRequestFields")
+    if _is_dict(add_fields):
+        add_inf = add_fields.get("inferenceConfig")
+        top_k = (
+            add_fields.get("topK")
+            or add_fields.get("top_k")
+            or (
+                (add_inf.get("topK") or add_inf.get("top_k"))
+                if _is_dict(add_inf)
+                else None
+            )
+        )
+        if top_k is not None:
+            invocation.top_k = top_k
+        if "seed" in add_fields:
+            invocation.seed = add_fields["seed"]
+
+    # system instruction
+    raw_system = kwargs.get("system")
+    if capture_content and _is_list(raw_system):
+        system_parts: list[MessagePart] = []
+        for item in raw_system:
+            if _is_dict(item) and "text" in item:
+                system_parts.append(Text(content=item["text"]))
+        invocation.system_instruction = system_parts
+
+    # input messages
+    raw_messages = kwargs.get("messages")
+    if capture_content and _is_list(raw_messages):
+        input_messages: list[InputMessage] = []
+        for msg in raw_messages:
+            if not _is_dict(msg):
+                continue
+            role = msg.get("role", "user")
+            parts: list[MessagePart] = []
+            content = msg.get("content")
+            if _is_list(content):
+                for block in content:

+                        if part is not None:

+            input_messages.append(InputMessage(role=role, parts=parts))
+        invocation.input_messages = input_messages
+
+    # tool definitions
+    tool_config = kwargs.get("toolConfig")
+    if _is_dict(tool_config):

threads.body: The try/except TypeError fallback and direct write to invocation._request_stream are unnecessary with the current util-genai SyncStreamWrapper signature and can mask real bugs. SyncStreamWrapper already accepts an invocation and sets _request_stream itself.

+class BedrockConverseStreamWrapper(SyncStreamWrapper[dict[str, Any]]):
+    """Wrapper for Bedrock converse_stream EventStream."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        stream: EventStream,
+        invocation: InferenceInvocation,
+        model_id: str | None = None,
+        *,
+        capture_content: bool = True,
+    ) -> None:
+        try:
+            super().__init__(stream, invocation=invocation)
+        except TypeError:
+            super().__init__(stream)
+            if hasattr(invocation, "_request_stream"):
+                invocation._request_stream = True
+        self._self_invocation = invocation

threads.body: This envlist entry expands the Bedrock latest test factor to Python 3.11–3.13, while other instrumentations in this repo consistently run latest only on the min/max versions (py3{10,14}). This likely increases CI runtime for one package without a clear repo-wide policy change.

This cassette file is not referenced by any test or conformance scenario in this package, so it adds repository weight without exercising behavior. Either add a test that uses it (to cover tool-call parsing error handling) or remove the cassette.
`reasoningContent` and the other non-text blocks are dropped, should we follow up on the other parts in a separate PR?

replies.body: I added it in here.. WDYT of the various supported block types here (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_ReasoningContentBlock.html) -- i left out audio / video blocks, but added parsing for document / image types.. not sure what the best approach is

we can add them as `GenericPart` and create semconv issue to add others. 

BTW, would you mind updating Blob (deprecated now) -> BlobPart and such?
Opened https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/488 and used GenericPart for them. Switched to `XPart` types too..

On second thought I wonder if it's worth adding these as GenericParts with just the `type` set, is that useful at all ? I don't think we will ever add raw audio / video to the telemetry, it's way too big.

Even a single image can be too big.. Google's telemetry API has a cap at 64KB for an attribute value for example.. Maybe we should be checking the size of `BlobPart`s (like mages) and leaving them out if they exceed 50KB or something like that..

`gen_ai.response.id` is available as `ResponseMetadata.RequestId`; the conformance scenarios declare it missing instead.

`response_model_name` should be dropped - Bedrock doesn't return a response model. If weaver complains in conformance, please add that one as  expected violation - it's useful input for semconv to document the case where a provider has no response model.

replies.body:
removed `response_model_name`.

I don't think `requestId` should be used for that. When you send an HTTP request to any AWS service, AWS's API gateway assigns a unique request tracking ID and returns it in the HTTP response header x-amzn-RequestId -- where as i think response id is like a model completion / continuation id (something generated by the model)
